purpose: Final bounded continuation decision, frozen before fault-injected collection
live_design: Two runs, baseline then namespace-key candidate. Same two-namespace workload. Ready Max threshold 10s. Measured job QPS 0.1, burst 1; setup QPS unchanged. Pause only the isolated cluster policy-controller process after probe dispatch and before policy creation. Resume one second after the second policy creation log. Always resume in finally. Maximum pause 90s, maximum run 300s.
rationale: Inject a known controller stall to separate policy creation timestamps while both flows remain denied. This is a controlled fault, not an observed spontaneous CNI defect or production rate.
primary: Baseline exits successfully despite first policy remaining without controller processing for >10s; candidate fails the same threshold and retains both identities.
evidence: Unmodified CLI logging, API policy timestamps, controller PID and pause/resume wall times, trace-level proxy results and emitted metrics. Confirm denied initial workload before accepting causal interpretation.
rejection: If pause occurs after first policy creation, if first-policy stall is <=10s, if proxy results missing, if controller restarts, or if outcomes do not match, retain inconclusive/failing run without tuning. No sweeps.
research_decision: Even a successful induced false pass does not establish novelty. Continue toward a journal only if prior-work comparison and independent-tool evidence support a broader distinct contribution. Otherwise archive as an engineering result and move research priority to the next literature-gated candidate.
